name: r3_floor_retroactive
description: REAL belief-drift from menhir history (retroactive_correction family). The recall similarity floor was BELIEVED to be a cosine threshold (~0.15, 'genuine matches >0.3') — that was the original code comment in scoring_service.py. It was later CORRECTED: the value the floor gates is graphiti's RRF node_reranker_score (rank_const=1 -> dual-method top = 2.0), so 0.15 is a RANK cut, not a cosine cutoff. Confirmed live by archolith-bench/scripts/probe_rrf_scale.py (RRF max 2.0). Provenance: scoring_service.py:50-55 (the correction is now in-code), R1 commit e8da67d, deferred-verification.md. Gold labels grounded in cited history; ctharvey confirmation is the stated pairing step. intent=current.

items.statement: The recall similarity floor (0.15) is a cosine-similarity threshold; genuine matches typically exceed 0.3.

evidence.note: the original scoring_service.py code comment asserted this
directly on-topic for a query about the floor
expired by the live RRF-scale measurement (probe_rrf_scale.py)

items.statement: The 0.15 floor gates graphiti's RRF node_reranker_score (rank_const=1, dual-method top = 2.0), so it behaves as a rank cut, not a cosine cutoff.

evidence.note: probe_rrf_scale.py measured RRF max 2.0 live on the throwaway graph

items.statement: BM25/file-linked candidates are exempt from the floor because their relevance is provenance, not cosine similarity.
The token estimator validation run used a different sampling window last month.
